purpose: Turns a single setting on or off, and the change applies the moment it is flipped. Use it in settings lists and panels where each row controls one independent option.

notFor.case: The choice only takes effect after the person presses Save or Submit.
The value can be partly selected, such as a parent row over a mixed group.
The person picks one option out of several.
Two or three short, mutually exclusive views or modes shown side by side.
Triggering a one-off action such as Delete or Send.

Checked=true.visual: Thumb at the end of the track; the track takes the action fill (Action/primary/default).

Checked=false.visual: Thumb at the start of the track; the track takes the muted fill (Surface/muted).

Default.visual: The track fill of its Checked value.

Hover.visual: The track moves to its hover role (Action/primary/hover when on, Surface/muted-hover when off).

Focused.visual: Focus ring around the track; the padding grows by the focus stroke so the thumb travel shortens.

Disabled.meaning: Cannot be changed and leaves the tab order.

a11y.keyboard: Tab reaches it unless disabled. Space or Enter toggles it (Radix Switch).
notes: Needs a visible label (SwitchGroup) or an aria-label supplied by the app; the component does not provide one.
On and off differ by thumb position, never by colour alone.
The track and thumb move with the motion role use-toggle; the focus ring with use-focus (recipes/motion.ts).

openQuestions: Reduced motion: should the thumb jump to its end with no slide, or keep a shorter slide?
Read-only: the Figma set has no read-only state. Does Switch need one (focusable, shows the value, cannot change), or is Disabled enough?
The io marks (IoVisible): Figma paints them Content/on-action when on and nothing when off; code takes the track role. Which is right? (finding PAR-001 Switch io)
